events.summary: Government arranged September elderly Aswesuma allowance payments for 695,818 beneficiaries.
112 Metro buses began operating across seven Western Province routes.
Treasury allocated Rs. 41 billion for a three-month fuel subsidy, limited to diesel.
Passenger rail services from Colombo to Peradeniya and Gampola will resume October 2 after repairs.
Repairs between Hatton and Kotagala are in their final stage ahead of year-end service resumption.
Tourism-zone upgrades are estimated to cost 15 million rupees, including access and visitor facilities.
The provincial department will provide 12.4 million rupees for Lakshapana Falls tourism development.
Ambagamuwa Pradeshiya Sabha will contribute 2.6 million rupees to tourism-zone upgrades.
Government proposed reserving 41 billion rupees for a three-month fuel subsidy.
Government gazetted 20 forests as reserves across six districts.
Parliament approved supplementary funding for electricity bill relief.
Parliamentary committee decided to appoint a subcommittee to examine principals’ salary disparities.
Cabinet memorandum submitted to recruit B.Ed. graduates directly into Grade 2 of the Teachers’ Service.
National Lotteries Board introduced the Ayubo lottery to raise public contributions for the National Health Development Fund.
Supplementary estimate proposed for electricity bill relief, funded by reallocating unused ministry provisions.
The first Southern Province battery storage system was officially connected to the national grid.
Engineers opened two Upper Kotmale Reservoir spillway gates after heavy rainfall.
Project cost is estimated at approximately Rs. 650 million.
Mahaiyawa tunnel construction reached approximately 80% physical progress.
Diyanajani floating solar plant was connected to the national grid.
Anuradhapura battery storage system joined the national grid.
Diyanajani floating solar plant was scheduled to open that day.
The first battery storage system was scheduled to open that day.
Rail passengers can buy tickets online through the Pravesha website and app.
Officials planned a new railway bridge near Kalu Bridge, with procurement expected to begin next year.
Emirates and Sri Lanka Tourism Promotion Bureau renewed their tourism promotion partnership through an MoU.
India-funded accident and emergency unit construction at Mannar District General Hospital was inaugurated.
The health minister said a CT scanner worth LKR 250 million would be provided to Mannar hospital by February.
Construction began on a four-storey medical officers’ residence complex at Mannar hospital.
The minister said construction of a new paediatric unit costing LKR 230 million could start this year.
The health minister said LKR 600 billion had been allocated to improve health services over two years.
Aswesuma September benefits totalling LKR 11.3 billion were arranged for credit to beneficiaries’ bank accounts.
Plan to increase annual medical student intake to 200 after the faculty building is completed.
Cabinet approved an additional Rs. 2.5 billion for Yala paddy purchasing.
Four hospital construction projects across Northern, North Central and Eastern provinces are estimated at Rs. 7.148 billion.
Cyclone-damaged railway restoration between Nawalapitiya and Thambiligala is underway.
ADB provincial health development plans for 2027 were allocated Rs. 6.7 billion.
ADB approved a $100 million loan for the provincial health programme.
ADB approved a $6.9 million foreign grant for the provincial health programme.
Coastal Conservation Department removed unauthorized fish stalls at Dewata Beach.
Excise Department filled vacancies through new recruitment and promotions in 2025 and 2026.
Stakeholders signed a three-year memorandum for a railway elephant-warning system.
People’s Bank launched a programme funding railway elephant collision prevention measures.
Coastal authorities ordered removal of 19 unauthorised structures along the coast.
SLBFE allocated 126 million rupees for 2027 loan-interest reimbursements.
A five-year inclusive recovery programme would support poor households in six districts.
The Kurunegala–Galewela section is scheduled to begin in November or December.
Construction of the Katuhathuwa–Ingiriya expressway is planned to begin in November or December.
The President directed the ministry to begin planning a Katunayake–Chilaw expressway.
The Kadawatha–Mirigama section is expected to be completed in May 2028.
The Pothuhara–Rambukkana section is expected to be completed in April 2027.
The Foreign Employment Bureau appointed 100 new staff to fill vacancies.
The second Metro bus depot began service in Kadawatha.
LKR 800 million in equity capital was allocated to Lanka Metro Transit for 2026.
Restoration between Rambukkana and Kadugannawa is nearing completion, with work expected to finish by September 15.
Restoration work is progressing on the Nawalapitiya–Gampola and Hatton–Nanu Oya railway sections.
Funding was allocated to Bimsaviya from 2007 through 2025.
Bimsaviya spending from 2007 through 2025 totalled LKR 4.45 billion.
The previous budget allocated LKR 3 billion for crop-loss compensation.
Officials said crop-loss compensation payments would begin the following week.
Authorities decided to introduce an integrated bus timetable on the Hatton–Kandy route.
Rambukkana–Peradeniya railway construction was nearing completion after cyclone damage.
Officials discussed digital ticketing, visitor limits, advance bookings and electric transport at Horton Plains.
Construction began on a four-storey cancer treatment unit funded by private donors.
The Agricultural and Agrarian Insurance Board introduced insurance for approved fruit crops.
Restoration began on 296 small irrigation tanks under a World Bank-supported programme.
Funding was set aside to restore six irrigation tanks in three districts.
Cabinet approved signing a complementary agreement to implement the Sri Lanka Sugarcane Project.
